summary: BC Assessment’s two earlier identities, which the gallery was missing: the British Columbia Assessment Authority’s outline-map identity, kept as dated pictures of it in use (no vector master has been found), and the italic BC Assessment wordmark, as the vector paths of its 2010 service plan. The supplied package’s report is package-README.md and its register source/package-source-register.json; source/ also holds the full 2021 logo row and the wordmark’s preview.

bc-assessment.notes: Three identities: the British Columbia Assessment Authority’s outline map of the province, in use by May 1982 and on its 1989–1990 notices; the italic BC Assessment wordmark with its comet rule, perhaps from the mid-1990s, when the short name was endorsed (1994) and the logo changed (1996), though no source dates it; and the full-colour mark of the 2015 rebrand, from the official media kit. The map is known only from pictures of it in use; its designer, colours and dates of introduction and retirement are not established.

openQuestions: An original vector master, standards sheet or designer for the outline-map identity.
The map identity’s introduction: the Authority dates from 1974, which does not date the symbol.
A full-colour specimen of the italic wordmark as the official mark specifies it (PMS 072 blue, the rule PMS 109 to PMS 032).

assets.label: BC Assessment: Italic wordmark and comet rule, with We Value BC
assets.publisher: British Columbia Assessment Authority, 2010/11–2012/13 Service Plan
assets.sourceLocator: PDF page 34: the wordmark and slogan, as vector paths
assets.dateNote: The service plan’s year. The Trade-marks Journal of 3 May 2000 published the wordmark as official mark 911,901; that is a publication date, not its introduction. The Authority’s corporate history records a logo change in 1996 and the board’s endorsement of the short name BC Assessment in 1994, which may be when this wordmark came in; no source here says so.
assets.notes: “BC Assessment” in italic serif over a rule, and “We Value BC” below: the wordmark between the outline map and the 2015 mark. The official-mark record names the typeface as Arrus and describes the rule as a comet running left to right, for action and progress.
assets.fidelityNote: The service plan’s own vector paths, extracted as SVG with the surrounding page clipped away: no tracing, redrawing or font substitution, no images and no live text. Blue (#00467f) as this publication printed it, converted from the PDF by its renderer; not an official colour. The official mark specifies blue lettering (PMS 072) and a rule blending yellow (PMS 109) into red (PMS 032), which this blue printing does not show. The cropped vector PDF is kept as a download.
assets.versionLabel: Blue, with We Value BC, 2010 service plan
